analysis:
Integration review of the PR found no security regression. The one functional change is in .github/workflows/release-provider.yml: qualify-sdk gets a job-level env DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT: prod (head ~lines 239-242), plus a comment edit at 181-182. The value is a static literal. It adds no secrets, expression interpolation, permissions or triggers. qualify-sdk keeps contents: read, has no secrets and no environment approval, and is not shown feeding signing or publication. build-provider still uses the resolved environment selector (head line ~183), and the signing job still smoke-checks the build-environment string (ENV_PREFIX/CLI_NAME) and the production designated requirement. A prod pin in the test lane therefore cannot make a dev or staging artifact look like prod, so official-build identity controls (T-034, T-054, A-017, A-011) are unchanged.

The other changes are docs/operations/provider-release.md (lines ~312-318), changelog.d/qualify-sdk-prod-identity.md, and scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py (lines 177-185). They describe or test the same change. The test edit is stricter: it requires exactly one mention of the variable, as a job-level env literal 'prod', and rejects the resolved-environment selector in qualify-sdk, so it cannot silently drift.

Unverified contracts, none of them establishing a vulnerability: (1) the provider-release-build action's lane=qualification logic is not supplied, so how it combines its `environment` input with the job-level env var is unknown; (2) provider-swift/Package.swift env-selection is not supplied, so the doc claim that an unset value compiles the dev identity on dev is unverified; (3) 12 integration-source units were omitted. Nothing in the changed lines touches the prefix-cache path (T-041), attestation, key custody or the coordinator protocol. No threat-model update is needed.
